Its si_dimension is L T^-1 and its dimension_vector [0,1,-1,0,0,0,0] matches the candidate exponents (I=0,J=0,L=1,M=0,N=0,T=-1,Theta=0). That record corresponds exactly to the ledger's delta variable and supports all coordinates of the proposed SI exponent vector.

The ledger names delta* as the boundary-layer displacement thickness. The KB record pq_displacement_thickness defines 'displacement thickness' (δ*) as an integral boundary-layer thickness representing the mass-flow deficit; its si_dimension is L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). This record directly matches the problem variable delta* and confirms the candidate exponents for length.

The ledger identifies theta as the boundary-layer momentum thickness. The KB record pq_momentum_thickness defines 'momentum thickness' (θ) as an integral boundary-layer thickness representing momentum deficit, with si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]. variables.physical_definition: The free-stream flow speed far from the boundary layer (external flow velocity).
The kinematic viscosity (momentum diffusivity) of the fluid.
Integral from the wall to the boundary-layer edge of the square of the local mean streamwise velocity with respect to wall-normal distance (∫ U(y)^2 dy).
Boundary-layer thickness at 99% of the free-stream velocity.
Boundary-layer displacement thickness (delta*), representing the effective vertical shift of the external flow due to the boundary layer.
Boundary-layer momentum thickness (theta), a measure of momentum loss relative to the free stream.
